title: Herod was troubled (Matthew 2:1–12)
hookLine: the wise men rejoice; the king, and all Jerusalem with him, are afraid
tomorrow: why is a woman from Genesis crying in Matthew?

lines: WHERE IS HE THAT IS BORN KING?
cards: A phone lights up with good news: the job, the yes, the baby on the way. Somewhere, someone else reads the same news and goes cold. Matthew's second chapter opens on a day like that.
Strangers from the east walk into Jerusalem and ask, out loud: "Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him."
They ask it a short walk from the palace of the man who already has that job.

teach.b: Matthew answers with two reactions, side by side. The palace first: "When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him." A king with soldiers and walls, shaken by a newborn.
He gathers the chief priests and scribes, who point him to Bethlehem, and he sends the strangers on, asking them to bring word back so he can come and worship too.
Then the road: "When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy." Same news. One side shaking, the other overjoyed.

In a house they find the child with Mary his mother, bow down, and open their treasures: "gold, and frankincense, and myrrh." One to tell a friend tonight: Matthew counts the gifts, never the visitors.
Three wise men is a later tradition.
Then the quiet ending: "being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way." No showdown with the king.
They simply don't take the old road home. Some readers hear a clever escape. Others hear more: people who have met the child don't go back the way they came.
Same star, same city. What differs is what each one has to lose.

how: Some churches remember the wise men at Epiphany, and in some homes and churches the figures of the wise men are added to the nativity scene only then.

games.q: a friend comes home from a summer away, kinder and calmer. at her first family dinner back, the old argument with her brother starts up. what would going home another way look like?
o: skip the fight she always joins, without announcing why.
give a speech about how much she's changed this summer.
act exactly as before, so nobody feels awkward.
games.why: the wise men didn't confront Herod or announce anything. warned in a dream, they simply took a different road home.

practice: Close your eyes and let one piece of good news come up, yours or someone else's: a change, a new person, a call to something bigger. Notice whether any part of you tightened when it arrived.
Don't scold that part; ask it quietly what it's guarding, and let the breath keep coming.

wordCard.voice: Herod was troubled. A king, and a whole city with him, shaken by news of a child, while strangers under a star rejoice.

orig.note: Greek: magi, the word behind Matthew's wise men from the east.
